headerPolicy: Every adapted file carries an inline attribution block pointing at the pin, copyright, and license file. Orca's source for the Grab Mode guest overlay is a self-contained JS string template; Nexus ports the algorithm to TypeScript module functions integrated into its existing preload overlay, so entries are type 'adapted' rather than 'copied'. Existing copyright notices inside copied code are preserved.

files.changeSummary: Incremental unique-selector strategy ported from Orca's Grab Mode guest overlay to TypeScript module functions (buildSelector, selectorPartFor, stableClasses, isUniqueSelector, nthOfTypeSuffix, looksHashy, UNSTABLE_CLASS_PATTERN). Orca emits a JS string injected via executeJavaScript; Nexus keeps its preload overlay architecture and adopts only the selector-construction logic, adapted to this project's secret redaction (redactBrowserText) and the isSensitive allowIds gate. A simple-css-ident id still resolves to '#id' (fast path, parity with prior behavior/tests). Produces shorter, more robust selectors by preferring stable class names over generated/hashed ones and only adding :nth-of-type when the partial selector is not yet unique.

In-page numbered annotation badges. Orca builds a JS string template injected into a dedicated world (worldId 1207) and mirrors viewport geometry back over prefixed console messages; Nexus ports the marker rendering/positioning algorithm (closed ShadowRoot host, badge at the element's bottom-center, rectPage-scroll vs rectViewport for isFixed markers, rAF-coalesced scroll/resize repositioning, visibility culling) to a TypeScript module in the pane's ISOLATED preload world, driven by the closed automation channel (design_set_annotation_markers). Markers carry geometry only — comments/element data never reach the page side. Strict page-side arg validation added (parseAnnotationMarkers).

Annotation model only, in the annotation section of browser-design.ts (BrowserPageAnnotation → BrowserDesignAnnotation): comment + intent (fix/change/question/approve) + priority (blocking/important/suggestion), 20-per-page cap, comment cap 2000 chars, annotations dropped on navigation. Orca persists annotations in the renderer Zustand store; Nexus moves authority to the main process: the renderer contributes only the typed note and the element context is the already-validated selection snapshot, frozen at annotate time. The grab payload extraction itself was NOT imported — Nexus keeps its own richer L0/L1/L2 selection context. Split from a former combined entry that also covered src/main/browser/design-session.ts.

Annotation store authority derived from the same upstream annotation model (src/shared/browser-grab-types.ts): Orca persists annotations in the renderer Zustand store; Nexus moves authority to the main process in design-session.ts — the renderer contributes only the typed note and the element context is the already-validated selection snapshot, frozen at annotate time. Split from a former combined entry that also covered src/shared/browser-design.ts.

Consolidated 'design feedback' prompt for a pane's annotations. Orca emits free-form markdown (page heading, per-annotation element label/selector/styles/HTML fences with backtick-run escaping); Nexus rebuilds the output on its untrusted-envelope prompt discipline (design-context-format.ts): page-derived data ships ONLY inside a bounded BEGIN/END_UNTRUSTED_PAGE_DATA JSON block (redacted + control-char scrubbed via safePageText), while the numbered user notes (trusted, typed in the IDE) and the per-intent instructions live outside it. Numbering matches the in-page badges. PT-BR intent labels; DESIGN.md attached as trusted block like design-send.
